claims.text: An ultrathin ALD-deposited Al2O3 layer is proposed between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The Al2O3 interlayer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve Cr-coating integrity.
The Al2O3-modified coating will retain oxidation resistance in both subcritical water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The baseline elemental Cr coating fails in high-temperature steam because of elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Approximately 300°C subcritical water is representative of normal reactor operating conditions.
Al2O3 will act as a stable and inert diffusion barrier during exposure to high-temperature steam.
Limiting interfacial atomic transport will preserve the structural integrity of the Cr layer.
Limiting interfacial atomic transport will preserve the oxidation performance of the Cr layer.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-modified cladding will exhibit improved oxidation resistance under both tested environments.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-modified cladding will exhibit improved coating integrity under both tested environments.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-modified cladding will exhibit reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion under both tested environments.
TGA or weight-change measurements can evaluate oxidation behavior.
Cross-sectional SEM and adhesion tests can assess coating integrity.
EDS mapping or SIMS can quantify Cr–Zr interfacial transport.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis frames the baseline Cr coating as protective under both service regimes before elevated-temperature interdiffusion causes failure, whereas the material_initial_state says it provides adequate protection in only one regime.
